messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? Usually standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention population mean 98.6. The standard deviation of the null hypothesis test might be the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null. That is sigma/sqrt(n). They gave sample standard deviation 1.4. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So about 0.221.

Alternatively, if they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For t-test, t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is standard error. So standard deviation of test statistic under null is 1 (for t distribution with df=39). But they might want the standard error. The phrase "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" is ambiguous. But likely they want the standard error of the mean. So answer: ~0.221.

We can also compute the p-value using the function. But they didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. So we compute standard error.

Thus answer: 0.221. Provide explanation.
